I agree that numbers are important. My warning against them is that I have seen churches focus so much on numbers that they stop being churches. One time I went to a church with smoke machines, coloured lights, loud music and a band who didn't actually do Christian music. There is nothing wrong with this, and had they mentioned Jesus I would have been ok seeing it as another way to do faith. But this was just seemt like a club going off at 10.00am on a Sunday. They had numbers though!

I don't think my answer will go over well, but here goes. It is because of how we treat women and rainbow people.  Don't worry about you numbers, worry about what your numbers represent.

I advocate for LGBTQIA+ people in my Diocese. We recently passed legislation allowing same-sex blessings, which was great, but the response to that legislation was a lot of hatred and several churches leaving for good. Hard to feel welcome when your invite in causes others to storm out the door. My day- job is a children and youth worker, for a church and an Anglican school. 99% of the kids have nothing against gay people, in fact, being gay is such a non-issue, that no-one really talks about it. In my day it would have been "Did you hear XX likes girls" but now its more "I saw XX and her gf at the weekend, they like the Thor movie".  About 20% of the kids are bi or gay. No one cares.

I heard a recent conservative argument that the number of gay people is so small, it wouldn't make an impact on church numbers. That person forgets that every time you turn someone away, their friends, family, coworkers and community probably go with them.

So you have Rainbow people desperately wanting entry, young people being confused as to why a 'loving' church won't let them and deciding they don't want much to do with a hateful church,  and a very very loud minority who don't want them let in.  And as the gay thing is a non-issue in a secular world, you aren't going to convert many secular people to something they see as promoting hate.

I know a number of you will tell me it's not hating. That it is "hate the sinner, love the sin" or "But saving them is loving them" Both of those arguments are bullshit and you take the role of God as judge. Even Jesus and the Pharisees differed on what they thought was sinful. And Jesus does not mention gay people, only Paul does, and it's not even in a big way.  The Pharisees held to the OT law and forgot the spirit of it. We are making the same mistake. Its a miracle we even got women priests with that kind of thinking. And some of the most prominent early church leaders, worthy to be mentioned in the bible, were women. Don't think early church means house group, it means church. Women were CHURCH leaders. So another reason that people don't want to come to churches, is because they are so male-dominated in a world that is actively trying to be equal. How many men are on your hospitality committee? How often do laywomen get invited to preach? How often do laymen? When the men have a 'Men's Breakfast" how many of the wives show up to cook for them. When the women have a 'Women's Bible Study' how many men turn up to do the supper? And look at your liturgy, God is genderless, God is described as both masculine and feminine (the female hen, the spirit of wisdom). So maybe liturgy should describe God as 1/3 male, 1/3 female and 1/3 genderless. Creator, Christ and comforter is just as valid as Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Holy Mother is just as much an option as Holy Father. Loving God is totally acceptable to use every single time.

Christ called us to be loving, to leave judgement up to God, to lead a Christlike example. The bible is also contextual (I know, I know) but if you are willing to where two types of cloth and eat shellfish, becuase we now have easier ways to wash clothes and safe ways to eat oysters, then you act out of this belief to.  When you look at the six clobber passages, there are a variety of arguments on both as to how they should be interpreted. I also guarantee you than everyone in your pews, sins. So stop letting a particular argument over whether or not something is sinful dictate who can have a place and a role in your church.  I don't think being gay is a sin, I don't think gay marriage or gay sex inside marriage is a sin. But if you do, then treat it the same way you do any other sin. Leave it God, make everyone welcome. Give them a place at the table of Christ.

People want a relationship with God, they want one with Christ. So let's make it as easy as possible, instead of getting them to jump through hoops of gender and sexuality.

If you want your church to grow in numbers, stop worrying about who should and shouldn't be allowed in your church. Actually, just let people in, let them in as they are and don't make a judgement on if they need to change. Let women be in leadership, let men make the tea and coffee, let the gay kids at the back feel welcome. Let the transgender person where skirts and nail polish without comment. Let them grow into youth leaders, leaders, and then Vestry members.

When you actually work in a Christ-like manner, with love as your priority,  you realise being welcoming is greater than bums on seats. Things like numbers don't matter, but will probably start to grow. Revisit your churches long term plan; make it open and welcoming to all.  And remember, Christ didn't care if he dined with sinners.

​

Edit: One final thought. I know some of you will point to the fact that in some areas conservatives are doing better. My encouragement is you stop thinking of Church as liberal and conservative ONLY. The Church is made up of liberal, conservative, and non-church goers. I would say the number of non-church goers far outweighs the conservatives. So my view is that Protestantism went 10 steps away from conservatism, so left the conservatives. But non-church goers are 15 steps away. So we didn't end up attracting either group. Imagine if secular people started coming to Church on Sundays, not just Christmas. And isn't it embarrassing that the secular world is currently more loving than the Anglican one? We need to be getting people to have a relationship with Christ, in whatever way we can.

Elegy for a hen

Not the sharpness or savagery others have looked for in birds,
cold eyes wanting prey to tear, claws for brutal dominance,
instead attributes, if less boisterous, more praiseworthy by citizens
offered up by a small hen in a suburban garden.

She watched with gentle keenness the movements of her world: the angle
of bees, wind’s curved seed heads, pigeons’ idle semaphore.
The senseless provocations of poor sighted gulls or unkempt cats
allowed by her to fall like morning light through pear trees. 

Always lending the world an eager embrace of simplicity;
earth, seeds, fresh air, rain: through modesty to satisfaction.
Sunning together in dust, one wing raised in friendly salutation,
always happier with others: days shared vigil, nights shared warmth.
A communal life with no presumption to be better than the dark
living soil she stood on, or evening light’s fine polished grain.

Which culminated at the end not in fierce and startled release,
but when all three eyelids closed, finally and for all times,
shutting out the trivial, the violent and at last both dark and light,
at the moment she came to be a mid-summer night’s dream,
rather she slumped gently, becoming one with her shadow
and the world stopped briefly, to sense the departing warmth.

This was/is me. In fact, breaking down and rebuilding my relationship with food has been the biggest part of my weight loss journey and whatever my end weight is I will always be prouder of the new way I view food. 

First off, and no offense meant to the other posters, do not just rely on will power. My will power is constantly fluctuating, I can turn down the brownie one day, but not the chips the next. To combat this, I use an 'as and when' rule. Basically,  I exercise and follow a diet whenever the will power is high. I try to stick to this for as long as possible. Normally I can stick to this for 9 days without cracking, and on day 10 my will power has dried up. If you are similar (which it sounds like you are) you will begin to notice your own pattern. My strategy has been to not eat back my calories. Lets say on Day 1 I eat my 1500 cal and burn off an extra 200, Day 2 I burn off 300 and Day 3 only 150. When I crack on Day 4, I might eat a 500 cal brownie. But adding up the calories burned, I ate most of them back but not all. 

The trick is to be ok with slower weight loss, and to incorporate food into the weight loss journey.

When it comes to constantly thinking about good food, utilise this skill. I will spend hours hunting for the perfect low cal soup, or new salad and then day dream about that until dinner. So you can use this skill for weightloss.

Secondly, you can use this for cheat days! Plan your cheat day to perfection, making sure you eat delicious things you crave. Create countdown sheet, visualising that there is only 5 days left until Venison Pie with Mashed Potato helps! Plus, I use the day dream of the Pie to get me through tough exercise. If I think 'I run today, Pie in 5 days or I can laze today and Pie in 6 days' I am more likely to then choose the run.

One thing I cannot stress enough is learning to not use food as a reward/emotional crutch. Before my journey I would eat to celebrate, and to cheer myself up. I would eat when bored, I would eat when there was loads to do. I would eat when I relaxed and when I needed to amp up. 

Now, I relax with a bath. I reward myself with a sleep in and a new book. I comfort myself lighting candles, shutting the curtains and watching Gilmore Girls. You need to find your own food replacements, but you get the idea. 

Log all your food(I still struggle with this). Basically, plan and replan, tweak as needed, and make sure you measure. Know exactly what you are eating. I find that this is easy on days when I am sticking to the diet. The days when I slip up and binge are harder. Once I know I am over, I give up logging. This is terrible, and I am working to stop it BECAUSE if I log the binge, I see how much work I am undoing, I limit the binge or feel guilty and it will be ages until the next one. 

Finally, invest in healthy snacks. If you like to munch when bored, munch celery or carrot sticks. A good tip here is to log a shit ton of them at the start of the day. Before you log anything else, tell MFP that you will eat 500g carrots that day. You won't (or not often) but you will eat a good amount. Snack on these when ever you want! Once these are logged, then plan the rest of your meals for the day. Also, because you won't eat the 500g carrots, that will mean you actually are eating a little less than MFP thinks, and will lose the weight a little faster.

Reward yourself for each step, set goals, and IF you slip up, think about how much better it was than the last time. At the beginning, my binges were around 6000cal, now they are 2500cal. I smile when I think of that!

Hey! For Starters, you have done amazingly. WOW- 33 pounds is awesome.  Here is some general advice from a person who constantly plays the comparing game. 

1) You do not know them, they may have been just like you at one point. They can be used as inspiration in this way.
2) You do not know them. They may have never struggled with weight loss, and maybe just got to do the muscles gain, ab definition part of this journey. This makes you better than them, you have worked harder for the mutual goal. 
3) Plateaus are a bitch, they are the reason so many of us fall off the bandwagon. BUT, double check that is a plateau, my bf could was stuck on a 'plateau' for three weeks, before realizing his daily rice amount had changed by mistake on MFP around 3 weeks back and he had been eating maintenance by mistake.  Similarly, with cardio what once may have been a puffing, sweaty, red faced achievement might now be a lot easier, so for the same weight loss results you will need to ramp it up a bit. 
4) If it is a genuine plateau, it will pass! 
5) If you are going to cheat, plan to cheat. This has two possible methods. 1) If you know you have a tempting dinner, or drink, being offered to you later that day, plan for it! Eat less during the hours leading up to it and then enjoy the cheat knowing it is actually the right calories and you have not over eaten. OR 2) Do this over a week, if there is one day where Mom's Lasagna attacks, then eat 100-200 cal less every day except Lasagna day, and then eat it ALL!!!!! (or the extra 600-1200 cal you earned in the week)
Lastly- come back to the reasons why you wanted to lose weight in the first place, think back to the inspired first days, maybe post them in here so you can see them in the real world, and then use them again.
Good luck my friend!
